levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: An assumption is named but it is not one the conclusion actually depends on.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: A load-bearing assumption is named and its effect on the conclusion is stated.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: A load-bearing assumption is named, tested against the scenario, and bounded.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: The parts of the plan contradict each other or do not add up.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: The plan adds up but one part is not connected to the rest.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: The plan adds up and each part is consistent with the others and with the constraint.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: The plan adds up, is internally consistent, and states what would break it first.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: A conclusion is stated with no figures behind it.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: Figures are quoted but the step from figure to conclusion is missing.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: The response shows which figures drive the conclusion and how.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: The response also says how large a change in a figure would flip the conclusion.

judgment.prompt: This household must hold two separate pools of money that it is not free to spend. Name them with their amounts, explain why keeping them separate matters, and describe how much of the seasonal earner’s $2,100 monthly pay is genuinely available to the household in a working month.
acceptableAnswerCriteria: Names both pools with figures: $3,024.00 set aside for the tax bill and $3,080.00 held to bridge the 4 off-season months.

Explains why they must not be pooled: the tax money is owed to someone else and spending it during the off-season creates a bill the household cannot meet, so a single combined balance will look adequate right up to the point it is not.

Computes or reasons to the available portion of the seasonal pay: $2,100 less the $378.00 tax set-aside is $1,722.00, and part of that must also go toward the off-season buffer, so materially less than $2,100 is genuinely spendable in a working month.
evidenceRequirements: Uses the $3,024.00 tax set-aside and the $3,080.00 off-season buffer, and refers to the -$770.00 monthly off-season position.
lookFors: The response keeps the two reserves distinct rather than adding them into one target.
The response recognises that the annual surplus of $4,536.00 is barely larger than the two reserves together.
judgment.commonMisconception: Treating money that has arrived in an account as money the household owns, when part of it is a tax liability and part is next quarter’s living costs.

nonDiagnosticGuard: Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

oracle.method: every fixed answer above was recomputed from the item's own stated scenario parameters, not transcribed
